### Israel's Sons in Exile
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/israels-sons-exile
Passage: 2 Kings 17:19-20
Points:
- The exile was the culmination of covenant curses warned against in Deuteronomy for persistent disobedience.
- Physical descent and religious outward forms cannot save anyone apart from genuine repentance and faith.
- God often deals with visible communities corporately, allowing faithful members to feel the fallout of national discipline.
- God's righteous judgment is purposeful and ultimately leads to the complete renewal of His people.
- Christ will ultimately make a final and perfect separation between authentic believers and mere professors.

### Bible Pathways 05/07/2002
Author: Bible Pathways
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-05-or-07-or-2002-1133416.html
Passage: 2 Kings 17:13-14
Points:
- God faithfully warned His people through His prophets to turn from evil and keep His commandments.
- Israel stubbornly hardened their hearts and refused divine instruction, bringing ruin upon the nation.
- An idol is anything or anyone that captures our supreme loyalty in place of God.
- Believers are urged to resist societal pressure toward moral compromise and cultural idolatry.
- Staying anchored in God's Word is the essential antidote to spiritual drift.

### Read the Bible: 2 Kings 17, Titus 3, Hosea 10, and Psalms 129–131
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/2-kings-17-titus-3-hosea-10-psalms-129-131/
Passage: 2 Kings 17:7-18
Points:
- The ultimate cause of Israel's fall was theological apostasy rather than merely military or political failure.
- Israel attempted secret idolatry, foolishly forgetting that nothing is hidden from God's sight.
- Pursuing empty idols inevitably resulted in the people themselves becoming spiritually empty and corrupted.
- Rejecting God's covenant warnings led inexorably to expulsion from His presence.
- The repeated failures throughout the monarchy highlight humanity's desperate need for a deeper, radical redemption.
